memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I also established my covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, where they resided as foreigners. Moreover, I have heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I have remembered my covenant." - Exodus 6:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God points back to a promise made centuries earlier to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob — men who lived their whole lives as foreigners in the very land they had been promised. They died without possessing it.

Now God says: I have heard the groaning, and I have remembered my covenant.

When Scripture says God remembers, it does not mean something slipped His mind. It means the moment has come to act on what He promised. God's memory is not recollection; it is faithfulness moving into action.

We should be careful here. The land promise was made under a specific covenant with a specific people, and we should not read our own hopes into it. God has not promised us a particular house, job or country.

But what carries across is this: God does not forget His promises, and He does not forget His people. Not one of them expired because of a long delay.

Every promise God has made to us in Christ is equally secure. Paul says all God's promises are Yes in Him (2 Cor 1:20).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which promise of God have I stopped believing because of how long I have waited?
2. Do I know what God has actually promised me in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that You never forget what You have promised. Anchor my hope in Your covenant faithfulness. Amen.
